examples.en: The picture on the wall is crooked.

tips: Also «crooked» (крива линија). «Крив сам» - I'm to blame, «Ко је крив?» - who is to blame?

examples.en: They let him out of prison.

tips: The word also means «constipation» in medical contexts: «Имам затвор».
Useful phrases: лежати у затвору - to be in prison, одлежати робију - to serve a sentence, пустити из затвора - to release from prison, побећи из затвора - to escape from prison.
«Такође» - also, too: «волим кафу, такође и чај». Do not confuse it with «исто» (the same) and «слично» (similar).
In everyday speech «и» is more common: «И ја.» «Доћи ћемо и следеће године.» «Такође» sounds more bookish and is rare in conversation.
Of a child, «жив» means lively, active, not only «alive».

examples.en: What do you expect from me?
We won't see each other until Monday.

note: «тек» of time: тек сада - only now, not before

examples.en: I lie in bed all day.

tips: «Постеља» - bedding, bed linen; «пресвући постељу» - to change the sheets. Кревет is the bed itself.

examples.en: Can I try on these pants?
Were you even listening to me?
The bus was full of people.

tips: Set phrases: пун месец - full moon, пун пара - flush with money, пун пунцат - chock-full. «Пуно» means «a lot» and also works as an intensifier, «very».

examples.en: I have a meeting at ten.
He threw the ball over the fence.

tips: Set phrases: «бацити се на нешто» - to throw oneself into something, «бацити удицу» - to cast a fishing line, «бацити се некоме под ноге» - to throw oneself at someone's feet.

related.en: to stop, to come to a halt

tips: The noun «лак» (m., gen. лака) means varnish, polish: «лак за нокте» - nail polish, «лак за косу» - hairspray, «лак за дрво» - wood varnish. It differs from the adjective in gender and declension.

examples.en: The doctors managed to save him.
I watch the news on TV.
Every parent worries about their children.

tips: «Ускоро» means soon (in the future), while «скоро» means «almost» or «recently»: «Скоро сам стигао» - I arrived recently.

examples.en: The police are investigating the murder.
The baby is asleep, keep it down.

tips: «Беба» is a baby up to a year old, «новорођенче» a newborn (up to 40 days); «малишан», «клинац» - a little kid, «клинци» - kids.
It means not only «done» but also «almost»: «готово два сата» - almost two hours, «готово цео дан» - almost all day. Often with a hint of exaggeration.
«Готово!» - There, it's done. «Готово?» - Is that all? «Није готово» - not finished yet.
More «almost»: «готово никад не излазимо заједно» - we almost never go out together, «то је готово бесплатно» - it's almost free. Related: «готов сам» - I'm done for.

examples.sr: Да ли је [мо̏гӯће] да је то истина?
examples.en: Is it possible that it's true?
We haven't seen each other since then.

note: не сме - must not, is not allowed
tips: «Не смем да једем шећер» - I'm not allowed to eat sugar (e.g. on doctor's orders), while «не могу да једем» - I can't eat (physically, or it doesn't work out).

examples.en: I tried to calm her down.
Do you want something to drink?
We're going for a drink after work.

examples.sr: Ово је [до̏ка̄з] да је био ту.
examples.en: This is proof that he was here.
He always gives me good advice.

note: To a person use «код»: идем код лекара

examples.en: I think about you all the time.

note: пасти на испиту - to fail an exam
tips: More than «to fall»: пасти на испиту - to fail an exam, пасти на памет - to come to mind, пасти у очи - to catch the eye, «плата ми је пала» - my pay has come in.
Colloquial: «пасти на нешто» - to fall for something, «пао је» - he got caught by the police, «пасти у несвест» - to faint.

examples.en: Sometimes I go to the movies.

note: «у улици» - on a given street (address); «на улици» - outside
tips: «У улици» is used of a specific street («живим у улици Иве Андрића»), «на улици» means in the open air, outside (close to «напољу»).

examples.en: He had a pistol in his pocket.
The water in the sea is warm.

tips: «Слатка вода» is plain still water, «кисела вода» is sparkling or mineral water. Not «sweet» and not «sour».
People answer the phone with «Хало!» or «Молим!». If you are the caller, greet after «Хало» and say who you are: «Добар дан, Марија је на телефону» - good day, this is Marija.

examples.en: He was like a brother to me.

forms: плашим се, плаше се; pf. уплашити се
note: плашити се + gen.; without се - to scare
tips: Takes the genitive: «плашити се мрака». Without «се» it means to scare: «плашити дете». A synonym is «бојати се».
Other reflexive verbs that take the genitive: «сећати се дана» (to remember the day), «стидети се грешке» (to be ashamed of a mistake), «чувати се ватре» (to beware of fire).

examples.en: You have to take it seriously.
Do you understand what I'm saying?
Now I understand why she left.
Why are you looking at me so strangely?
He pulled a wallet out of his pocket.
You won't get away with it this time.

note: извући се - to wriggle out of it

tips: Чувати - to keep, protect, guard, look after (a child, a sick person): «Чувај се!» - take care, «пас чува кућу» - the dog guards the house. Past «чувао сам» - not to be confused with «чуо сам» (I heard).
Also to babysit: «хвала што нам чуваш дете» - thanks for looking after our child; «чувати стоку» - to keep livestock.
«Ужина» is a light snack, e.g. in the afternoon: «ужинати» means to have a snack, not dinner.

examples.en: Where do you suppose he is?
I didn't mean to hurt you.

tips: Not only physical: «повредио си је» - you hurt her. It is also said of feelings: «повредити некога» - to hurt, offend someone.
Three senses: opportunity, chance; occasion, pretext; circumstances and conditions (економске прилике, plural). «Одлична прилика да скијамо» - a great occasion to go skiing.
«Стицај прилика» - a coincidence of circumstances; «прилике» in the plural - circumstances, conditions.
«Кола» is a neuter plural: «Нова кола су лепа», «Где су ми кола?»; the singular is «ауто» (m.). There is also «кола» (f. sg.) - cola: «Ова кола је хладна».
Not «wheels»: a wheel is «точак», pl. точкови. Also «спаваћа кола» - sleeping car, «Велика кола» - the Big Dipper.
The plural «избори» means elections (plural only): «Избори су заказани за јесен» - the elections are scheduled for the fall.

meanings: to be missing, to be lacking
tips: The structure is reversed: the person missed is the subject (nominative), the one who misses is in the dative: «недостајеш ми» - I miss you, «недостајем ти» - you miss me. Colloquially also «фалиш ми».

examples.en: I can't see clearly without glasses.
My father is in the hospital.
They took him to the hospital.
In the morning we set off on a trip.
We have to leave the building.
The store is next to the post office.

tips: Поред = 1) next to, 2) in addition to (поред тога - besides that), 3) compared to (поред њега изгледаш као џин - next to him you look like a giant), 4) despite (поред свега труда - despite all the effort). Always with the genitive.
«Никакав» declines like an adjective («никакву идеју», «никаквог разлога») and goes with a negation: «немам никакву идеју» - I don't have any idea.

examples.en: I'm waiting for you in front of the house.
A long road lies ahead of us.
Why are you running away from me?

note: бежати - to run away; plain «to run» is трчати

examples.en: What kind of music do you like?
This is some kind of game.

note: нека врста - a kind of, sort of

examples.en: Don't waste your time on him.
We have to solve this problem.
I decided to stay at home.

tips: «Решити се» + genitive without a preposition: to get rid of something («Решио сам се ненужних ствари»). «Решити се да» + present: to make up one's mind: «Решио се да оде».

forms: смејем се, смеју се; pf. насмејати се
note: смејати се + dat. - to laugh at
tips: Takes the dative, with no preposition: «смејемо се његовој шали» - we laugh at his joke.
«Осмехнути се» - to smile. «Шта се смејеш?» - what are you laughing at? «Није смешно» - it's not funny. «Смејем се, а плакао бих» - I laugh, but I feel like crying.

examples.en: Have you ever been to Paris?

examples.sr: Ово је најбоља пица коју сам [и̏када] јео.
examples.en: This is the best pizza I've ever eaten.

examples.sr: Наш [ста̑н] има три собе и терасу.
examples.en: Our apartment has three rooms and a terrace.
The king lived in a large palace.
He acts as if he were a king.
Where are those damn keys of yours?
They say this house is cursed.
Drive slowly, the road is slippery.
Take it easy, we have plenty of time.

tips: Not just «slowly» but a way of life: calmly, without rushing. «Полако!» - take it easy, don't rush.

examples.en: My brother is strong as a bull.
I wrote her a long letter.
Can you write down the address for me?

examples.sr: Кад сам био [дѐча̄к], живео сам на селу.
examples.en: When I was a boy, I lived in the country.
I don't know where he came from.
I've never seen a car like this.
I don't like weather like this.
A police officer stopped us on the road.
My brother is a police officer.
The victim was taken to the hospital right away.

examples.sr: Родитељи су поднели велику [жр̑тву] за нас.
examples.en: Our parents made a great sacrifice for us.

forms: слажем се, слажу се; pf. сложити се

examples.en: My brother and I get along well.

note: Not to be confused with «слагати» (pf. of «лагати») - to lie
tips: With «са» + instrumental it means «to get along»: «Да ли се добро слажете у породици?». Without a preposition - «to agree».

forms: украдем, украду; past украо; impf. красти

examples.en: Thieves stole a car in front of the building.
He's out of town this week.
The situation is completely out of control.

examples.sr: У суботу идемо на [за̀баву] код Марка.
examples.en: On Saturday we're going to a party at Marko's.
I don't have the money for a new phone.
Steam is coming out of the pot.

tips: Also a hundredth part of a dinar, like a cent: «99 динара и 99 пара». The coins are long gone, but the word appears in prices. Singular пара - small change, plural паре - money. Synonym: «новац».
The plural «паре» is colloquial but not slang: «пун пара» (rich), «тврд на пари» (stingy), «ни пребијене паре» (not a penny).
«Паметан» also means knowing about something: «нисам паметан» - I can't make sense of it, «имам паметнија посла» - I have better things to do.

examples.en: Every day I start with coffee.
The attack took place late at night.
He had a panic attack on the plane.
I have no idea where he is.
Freedom is a very broad concept.
Can you explain this to me?
I explained everything to her from the beginning.
Last night we were at the movies.
The police detained him at the border.
The city has almost a million inhabitants.

forms: појавим се, појаве се; impf. појављивати се

examples.en: He suddenly appeared in the doorway.
She didn't show up for work.

meanings: to lead through, to show around
forms: проведем, проведу; past провео; impf. проводити

examples.en: We spent the summer at the seaside.

examples.sr: Желим да [про̀ведем] више времена с децом.
examples.en: I want to spend more time with the kids.
She broke up with her boyfriend.

note: прекинути с неким - to break up with someone

examples.en: We spent a wonderful day at the lake.

note: An adjective, not a piece of furniture

examples.en: Here you go, this is for you.

note: «изволите» - polite «here you are» or «may I help you?»

examples.sr: Хтео сам да дођем, [но̑] нисам могао.
examples.en: I wanted to come, but I couldn't.
The house is small but comfortable.

note: Bookish; in speech «али» is more common

examples.sr: Кажу да у тој кући живи [ду̏х].
examples.en: They say a ghost lives in that house.
There's a good spirit in our team.
This ticket is valid for a month.

tips: «Важи!» - deal. «Ма важи» - ironic: yeah, sure. The basic meaning is to be valid («лична карта важи до...»); «важити за» - to be regarded as something.
In conversation: «Видимо се у пет? - Важи.» Literally «it holds». «Важи за све» - it applies to everyone, «важи до петка» - valid until Friday.
Takes «у» + locative, and the preposition is required: «Уживам у музици», «Уживајте у овом граду!», «уживам у лепом времену, у спорту».

examples.en: She bought a black dress for the celebration.

related.en: to turn black; to get tanned

tips: Many figurative uses: црно вино - red wine, црни лук - onion, црни петак - Black Friday (a sale) or a bad day, црне бриге - heavy worries. «Какав црни...!» - what on earth...!

examples.en: In the evening I like to read in bed.
He hit me for no reason.
I banged my head on the door.
Go to hell with your advice!
Let me know as soon as you arrive.
As soon as he walked in, everyone went quiet.
I transferred the money to your account.

note: водити рачуна о + loc. - to take care of, to look after
tips: Also «водити рачуна» - to be careful, to take into account: «Води рачуна!» - be careful, take care.
It means both a bill and a receipt; a current account is «жиро-рачун». A payment slip is «уплатница», a receipt for payment is «признаница».
«Отворити рачун» - to open a bank account. The score of a match is «резултат», not «рачун».

examples.en: Hurry up, the train is leaving!

examples.sr: Морамо да [по̀журимо] ако хоћемо да стигнемо.
examples.en: We have to hurry if we want to make it.
Wake me up at seven, please.
I woke up very early this morning.
Sit in front next to me.
He works as a real estate agent.
The secret agent followed the suspect.
I'm still waiting for an answer from them.
Do you know the answer to this question?
I have no more strength for this.
The wind blew with great force.

note: имати на уму - to keep in mind

examples.en: She learned to ride a horse.

tips: Of a person it means a fool: «Не буди коњ, размисли мало». Vocative - «коњу».

examples.en: You look funny in that hat.

examples.sr: Деца су истрчала [на̏поље] да се играју.
examples.en: The kids ran outside to play.

tips: «Напоље» is a direction, «out, outside» («изаћи напоље» - to go out); «напољу» is a place, «outdoors, outside the house».

examples.en: Our plane takes off at six.
Take off your coat and sit down.

tips: «Скинути» - to take off (clothes, shoes, glasses) and to undress someone: «скини дете»; «скини се» - to get undressed. Imperfective - «скидати».
Also: to download («скинути песму са интернета»), to cross off a list («скинути са листе»), to copy someone's voice or manner. Context decides.

examples.sr: Да ли вам [сме̏та] ако отворим прозор?
examples.en: Do you mind if I open the window?
Music distracts me while I work.

note: + dat.: смета ми - it bothers me

examples.en: The police are still looking for the killer.
The killer escaped through the window.

note: Masculine, but declined like words in -а

examples.sr: С [о̏бзиром] на кишу, остали смо код куће.
examples.en: In view of the rain, we stayed home.

examples.sr: Ни под којим [о̏бзиром] не отварај врата.
examples.en: Under no circumstances open the door.

note: с обзиром на - considering; без обзира на - regardless of
tips: Almost always in set phrases: «без обзира на» (regardless of), «с обзиром на» (considering), «узети у обзир» (to take into account), «не долази у обзир» (out of the question), «имати обзира» (to show consideration for someone).

examples.sr: Нови [за́кон] ступа на снагу у јануару.
examples.en: The new law comes into force in January.
The cat is sleeping under the table.
Give me a little time to think.
They have a son and two daughters.
My daughter is in first grade.
She has a very beautiful voice.
Don't raise your voice at me!
You look kind of sad today.
Where did I leave my keys?
Persistence is the key to success.
The bullet hit him in the leg.
I bought two tickets for the concert.
Look at the map to see where we are.

tips: «Карта» - any ticket (plane, bus, match, concert): «Имам две карте». An admission ticket specifically is «улазница».
Besides a ticket, «карта» is also a map and a playing card. For a concert or theater ticket «улазница» is more common, though «позоришна карта» is also said.

examples.en: Last year we were in Greece.
We saw each other last weekend.

tips: In military and official contexts «позив» is a summons, a call-up («позив за војску»); in everyday speech it is more often a call or an invitation.

examples.sr: Имам лош [о̏сећа̄ј] у вези с тим.
examples.en: I have a bad feeling about it.
He lost feeling in his fingers.
If they catch us, we're done for.

tips: «Готова ствар» - a done deal, the matter is settled. «Готова јела» - ready meals (from a shop). «Готов новац» - cash.

examples.en: Since it's raining, we'll stay home.

note: «Пошто је ово?» - how much is this?
tips: Also «after» («пошто је завршио»), «since, seeing that» («пошто тако кажеш») and, colloquially, «how much»: «Пошто су јабуке?» - «По сто педесет динара кило» (150 dinars a kilo).
For «why» use «зашто» (colloquially «што»), not «пошто».

examples.en: This face looks familiar to me.

tips: «Познат по» + locative - known for something: «Србија је позната по специјалитетима», «Нови Сад је познат по фестивалу».

examples.sr: Синоћ сам изашао са [дру̏штвом] у град.
examples.en: Last night I went out on the town with friends.
We live in a modern society.
His fight against the illness has lasted for years.
I like to socialize with my colleagues.
Who do you hang out with at school?

tips: Broader than «to be friends»: to socialize, to spend time together («дружим се са породицом»), also to be on good terms with something («дружити се са природом», «са телефоном»).

examples.en: The guests come in through the main entrance.
I got a letter from my grandmother.
They elected him president of the club.

examples.sr: Не могу да [за̀мислим] живот без тебе.
examples.en: I can't imagine life without you.
I'm waiting for you in front of the building.
The car is parked in front of the house.
He put the suitcase down on the floor.

examples.sr: Био је то [ду̏г] и тежак дан.
examples.en: It was a long, hard day.
I help Mom in the kitchen.

tips: The imperfective of «помоћи»: помажем, imperative «помагај!»: «Нико ми не помаже» - nobody helps me, «нико ти није помагао» - nobody helped you.

examples.en: We had a wonderful time at the seaside.

tips: «Дивна» also fits a person's character: «ти си дивна особа» - you're a wonderful person. For looks, «прелепа жена» (a beautiful woman) is stronger.

examples.en: I work every day, except Sundays.
The police found traces of blood.
He still hasn't replied to my message.
Good evening, may I help you?
We spent a lovely evening together.
Many people work on weekends too.

examples.sr: [И̏ако] је болестан, дошао је на посао.
examples.en: Although he is sick, he came to work.
We went out even though it was raining.

tips: «Иако» introduces a concession: «Иако је касно, идемо». Not to be confused with «као» (like, as).

examples.en: I found myself in an awkward situation.
Don't worry, everything is under control.
The driver lost control of the vehicle.

tips: «Контрола» is feminine: «строга контрола».
«Имати контролу над» + instrumental: «над ситуацијом», «над емоцијама».

examples.en: The brain uses a lot of energy.

meanings: to set off, to start moving

examples.en: We set off early tomorrow morning.
The Earth moves around the Sun.
I need a little more information.

examples.sr: Где могу да добијем [информа̀ције] о возовима?
examples.en: Where can I get information about the trains?
Will you sell me your bike?
That doesn't interest me at all.

note: занима ме - I'm interested (literally, it interests me)

examples.en: He was accepted to the university.
Last night I drank too much beer.

tips: Colloquially also a traffic light: «код другог светла скрените лево» - turn left at the second light (more often «семафор»).

examples.en: She accepted his invitation to dinner.
We have to accept the truth.
How often do you wash your hair?

tips: Usually singular: «Коса ми је дуга» - my hair is long. The same word also means a scythe.

examples.en: Let's go for coffee after work.

tips: «Кафа» is feminine: «јака кафа», «моја кафа», «добра кафа».
When ordering, «Може кафа?» has the coffee in the nominative (not «кафу»). The accusative «кафу» is needed after «молим» and «желим».

examples.en: He was elected president of the club.
We traveled in a large group.
I'm just kidding, don't be mad!

forms: pl. будале; of a man: тај будала
note: Of a man it takes masculine agreement: «тај будала»
